title: Rear Suspension: Find the Part and Its Job
introduction:
The rear suspension makes more sense when each part has a job. Springs support the load and store energy as the wheels move; shock absorbers resist that motion so it settles. I think of the spring as an energy savings account and the shock as the withdrawal limit: storing energy and controlling its release are different tasks.

Use the callouts and adjacent table together. In the drawing, the orange coils sit beside the tall blue shocks. The blue stabilizer bar crosses behind the gray subframe, while the arms and links connect the subframe to the wheel knuckles. At each outer end, distinguish the knuckle that carries the hub from the hub that rotates and the studs that secure the wheel.

I follow the table’s leader lines carefully around the crowded lower-arm area; color helps navigation, but it is not a diagnosis. The toe link helps control the wheel’s direction viewed from above, while the upper and lower arms guide wheel travel. This reference identifies components and their relationships. It does not provide lifting, inspection, alignment, fastener-release or replacement instructions.
